diff:
--- a/slugs.py
+++ b/slugs.py
@@ -1,5 +1,10 @@
 import re
+import unicodedata
 
 
 def slugify(value):
-    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", value.lower()).strip("-")
+    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", value)
+    without_marks = "".join(
+        ch for ch in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(ch)
+    )
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", without_marks.lower()).strip("-")

contract_tests: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_precomposed_accented_words_transliterate - asserts slugify("Café déjà vu") == "cafe-deja-vu" (exact str input, exact str output).

tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_decomposed_matches_precomposed - asserts slugify("cafe\u0301 de\u0300ja\u0300 vu") == slugify("Café déjà vu") == "cafe-deja-vu" (decomposed combining acute/grave input matches precomposed).
tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_ascii_word_separation_preserved - asserts slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world" (existing ASCII behavior preserved).
tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_dashes_trimmed - asserts slugify("  --Café--  ") == "cafe" (leading/trailing dashes trimmed after transliteration).
tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_result_is_ascii_str - asserts isinstance(slugify("Café déjà vu"), str) and slugify("Café déjà vu").isascii() (output type and ASCII-only contract).
patches.rationale: The issue requires slugify to transliterate Unicode combining accents before producing lowercase ASCII slugs. The original implementation only lowercases and replaces non-[a-z0-9] runs with dashes, so accented characters like é are stripped entirely (e.g. 'Café déjà vu' -> 'caf-d-j-vu'). The fix normalizes the input to NFD, strips combining marks, then applies the existing ASCII word-separation and dash-trimming logic. This preserves existing behavior for ASCII inputs and makes decomposed 'cafe' + combining acute match precomposed 'café'.
